A decorative color with no light capture
A green pigment in leaves that takes in light and allows photosynthesis
Water alone holding all the plant's energy

It is found in chloroplasts.
What is the role of roots in a plant?
Roots capture sunlight for all parts of the plant.
Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil to feed the plant.
Roots are where animals find shelter during cold weather.
Roots release seeds into the surrounding soil.
Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil. These travel upward through the stem and into the rest of the plant, supporting its growth.
Roots grow underground and anchor the plant in the soil.
Water and minerals travel from the roots upward through the stem.
What is the role of the stem in a plant?
The stem produces food for the plant by using sunlight.
The stem supports the plant and carries water and nutrients to other parts.
The stem is where animals find shelter during winter.
The stem absorbs carbon dioxide directly from the soil.
The stem supports the plant and acts like a pipe, carrying water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
The stem connects the roots to the leaves.
Water absorbed by roots travels through the stem to reach the leaves.
What is the role of leaves in a plant?
Leaves help animals see where to find food.
Leaves capture sunlight for photosynthesis and produce oxygen as a result.
Leaves act as the lungs for animals that live inside the plant.
Leaves carry water through the plant instead of the stem.
Leaves are the plant's food factory. They capture sunlight and use it, along with water and carbon dioxide, to make food through photosynthesis. Oxygen is released as a byproduct.
Leaves contain chlorophyll, which captures sunlight.
Photosynthesis produces food for the plant and releases oxygen into the air.

The entire plant, including all its roots and flowers, appears instantly.

When conditions are right — enough water, warmth, and sometimes light — a seed germinates. A small root and shoot grow out of the seed and develop into a new plant.

Seeds need water, warmth, and sometimes light to germinate successfully.
How does a fruit form on a plant?
A seed falls to the ground and turns directly into a fruit.
A fruit develops from the flower after pollination.

Water flowing up through the root forms the fruit directly.

Pollination is the transfer of pollen that fertilizes the flower.
The fertilized flower develops into a fruit that holds and protects the seeds.

A description of liquids with no solid or gas

States of matter are the forms matter can take: solid (hard shape), liquid (flows), or gas (spreads out).
Water can exist in all three states.
Temperature can change the state of matter.
What is melting?
Heating with no change of state
A change from solid to liquid
Cooling that makes ice instead of water
Freezing a liquid into a solid
Melting is the change from solid to liquid—for example, ice turning into water when heated.
Melting happens when temperature rises.
Every material has its own melting point.
What is freezing?
Cooling with no change to a solid
A change from liquid to solid
Heating that melts ice into water
Melting a gas into a liquid
Freezing is the change from liquid to solid—for example, water turning into ice when cooled.
Freezing happens when temperature drops.
Every material has its own freezing point.
What is evaporation?
Heating with no liquid turning into air
A change from liquid to gas
Cooling that gathers water vapor into liquid
Only melting a solid into a liquid
Evaporation is the change from liquid to gas—for example, water turning into water vapor when heated.
Evaporation increases as temperature rises.

What is condensation?
Cooling with no liquid droplets forming
A change from gas to liquid
Heating that fully spreads water vapor away
Only melting ice into water

A material that allows heat or electricity to pass through it easily.

Plastic — it conducts electricity better than any metal.

Metals such as copper and iron are common conductors.

A pure metal with free electrons
Thin glass as a strong electricity conductor
